issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s acquisition of only some co-owner landlords’ interests does not determine the tenancy by merger, and the tenant remains subject to rent-control obligations.
material_facts: The occupants held the building under a continuing lease.
They acquired the rights of some, but not all, of the co-owner landlords.
The rights of the remaining co-owner landlords did not vest in the occupants.
The landlords obtained a rent-control order directing the occupants to deposit rent, and the occupants challenged that order on the ground that the tenancy had ended by merger.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy was not determined by merger because the occupants acquired only some co-owner landlords’ rights. They remained tenants and were bound to comply with the rent-control requirements, including the rent-deposit order; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 105 and 111(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, a lease is determined by merger only when the lessee’s and lessor’s interests in the whole property vest simultaneously in one person in the same right, with no intervening estate. Acquisition of only part of the reversion, including the rights of a co-owner, is insufficient. Section 44 does not vest the entire property interest in the acquiring tenant, and Section 109 permits an assignee of the reversion to exercise the lessor’s rights but does not itself extinguish the tenancy. The Court approved T. Lakshmipathi v. P. Nithyananda Reddy and the approach in India Umbrella Manufacturing Co. v. Shagabandei Agarwalla; it held Abul Alim v. Sheikh Jamal Uddin Ansari incorrectly decided on this point, and distinguished Jagdish Dutt v. Dharam Pal because Section 111(d) was not applied there. The principle is also supported by Faquir Baksh v. Murli Dhar, Badri Narain Jha v. Rameshwar Dayal Singh, and Puran Chand v. Kirpal Singh.

predicates.rent_deposit_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a direction to deposit rent in a rent-control matter.
predicates.tenant_acquired_partial_reversion: The tenant acquired the rights of only some of the landlords in the property.
predicates.co_owner_interests_remained_outstanding: The interests of other co-owner landlords remained outstanding and did not vest in the tenant.

issues.definition: When a tenant appealing a rent-deposit direction has acquired only some landlords’ interests and other co-owners’ interests remain outstanding, the tenancy continues and the tenant remains subject to rent-control obligations.
